intl.items.title: European Robot Soccer Cup - Croatia
intl.items.subtitle: European Vice-Champion
intl.items.text: Second place at the European robot soccer competition in Croatia, competing against a multitude of international teams. This competition features autonomous robots playing football, with technical challenges in artificial intelligence, computer vision, and real-time control. My technical contribution: developed a predictive goalkeeper strategy in Python, implemented computer vision algorithms for ball tracking, trajectory prediction based on opponent robots' orientation, optimized reaction time to maximize saves. Skills developed: international teamwork (4 people), stress management in competition, real-time problem-solving, leadership and quick decision-making.

timeline.title: Vision
timeline.description: Become an expert at the intersection of aerospace and quantum.

market: The quantum computing sector is experiencing significant growth as a strategic field. The market reached USD 1.07 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 8.6 billion by 2027 [1].
Industry-wide, quantum-related roles have grown substantially, with documented talent shortages indicating strong long-term demand [2].
In aerospace specifically, quantum applications are moving from research to practical implementation, as demonstrated by industry leaders like Boeing and Airbus [3][4].
why: This intersection represents a unique opportunity to combine emerging technology with proven real-world applications.
The field holds strategic importance for aerospace and defense sectors.
It requires both deep technical expertise and continuous learning.
Clear career progression exists in a growing industry with sustained demand.
references: LinkedIn Workforce Insights, "Quantum Technology Job Market Overview," 2024.
Airbus, BMW Group, and Quantinuum, "Quantum Computing for Aerospace Applications," 2023.
